blocks.title: Network architecture
blocks.text: Network architecture is the overall design of a computer network: how computers, servers and other devices are arranged, and how data is transmitted across the network.

blocks.alt: Top panel: a computer, laptop, phone and printer each joined by a line to a switch; the switch joins a router, and the router joins a cloud labelled Internet. Bottom panel: the data HELLO CLASS XII is split into three numbered packets, the packets travel over cables or radio signals and may arrive out of order, and the receiver puts them back together as HELLO CLASS XII.
blocks.caption: Devices sharing data through a network in packets (original diagram after Figs 1.1 and 1.2).
blocks.long_description: The switch links the devices of one network and the router links that network to others such as the Internet. Large data is cut into small numbered packets, which lets many devices share the same lines.

blocks.text: Network architecture includes the hardware, the software and the communication rules. A good architecture helps the network work efficiently and supports its future expansion (Fig 1.2).

items: The data is broken into small units called packets for transmission.
The packets travel through cables or wireless signals.
Network devices guide each packet to the correct destination.
The receiving device reassembles the packets into the original data.

blocks.text: This process allows smooth and fast communication: many devices can share the same links, and a lost packet can be sent again without resending everything.

blocks.title: Class activity
blocks.text: Look at pictures or names of devices and match each device name with its function; then discuss the answers.

blocks.prompt: What is network architecture, and what three things does it include?
blocks.explanation: It is the overall design of a network: how devices are arranged and how data is transmitted. It includes hardware, software and communication rules.

blocks.prompt: Why is data broken into packets before it is sent?
blocks.explanation: Small packets can share the network's links with other traffic, can each be guided to the destination, and can be resent individually if lost; the receiver reassembles them into the original data.

items: Architecture: arrangement of devices plus how data moves; hardware, software and rules.
Data is sent as packets and reassembled at the receiver.
